newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps jump on US tropical storm, heatwave.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps jump on US tropical storm, heatwave.

text.p: European oil swaps jumped higher on Thursday as the market stepped up a gear and screen crude rallied amid concerns about tropical storm Danny in the U.S. Gulf and an eastern U.S. seaboard heat wave.
Strong NYMEX gasoline continued to play a dominant role.
Brent CFDs firmed by up to 17 cents or so, gasoline swaps rose $3-4 a tonne, naphtha was up $1.50 while fuel put on around $2-3.

July 21-25 Brent CFDs shot up to +5 cents against September from -12 cents while July 28-August 1 firmed to -7 cents from -15 cents. August 4-8 went to -10 cents from -19 cents and August 11-15 gained to -13/14 cents from -20 cents against September.
A July 21-25 traded at - 2 cents against September in the morning and later July 28-August 1 went at - 7 cents. Also in the afternoon August 4-8 traded twice, once at -12 cents and once at -8 cents.

Gasoline rose about $4 a tonne as the market reacted to galloping NYMEX mogas. August paper traded at $193.50 and September was valued around $181 with activity focused on naphtha/gasoline spread trading. October was seen around $187.50.
Physical cargoes were offered ex NWE at high fob quotes +$2 and cargoes were bid into Hamburg at $194/195. A 20kt regular cargo was thought sold around cif high quotes +2.
Fuel swaps were around $2-3 stronger with the U.S. heat wave on the eastern seaboard supporting low sulphur fuel buying interest.

Heavy fuel saw July trading at $87.50 and August at $88.50 in the morning before the market really took off. By late afternoon August had traded at $89.50 twice and September was pegged around $90.25 having traded at $90. Further out Q4 traded at $94 and Q1 at $97.
The hi-lo spread widened as a hot U.S. contemplated the need for fuel to power air-conditioning. August was valued around $97.25 with September about $1 stronger.

Naphtha swaps were $1.50 higher on the front month, backed by tight physical supplies and higher physical deal numbers. August was seen at $190.50-191 with the September backwardation widening to around $3 and October seen $1.50-2 behind September.
